clue.text: An educated person, to a certain degree …

definitions.text: An educated person, to a certain degree

blocks.note: surface reading: someone with some schooling, more or less
setter's reading: someone holding a particular university degree, the first one awarded

explanation.walkthrough: 'To a certain degree' reads as 'somewhat', but it means holding a specific academic degree, as a BA or BSc holder is a bachelor.
explanation.definitionFit: A bachelor is a graduate holding the first-level university award, so an educated person by qualification.

clue.text: Well, out of bed for liquid lunch perhaps

blocks.note: 'well' and 'so' both open a remark: 'Well, what now?'
someone out of bed is up

explanation.surface: Someone recovering after a late rising, choosing a drink-heavy midday meal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Liquid lunch' usually means drinking alcohol at lunchtime; here it is taken literally as a lunch you drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Soup is a lunch eaten as a liquid, so it is an example of a literal liquid lunch, flagged by 'perhaps'.

clue.text: Won points, so made the cut

blocks.note: first meaning: gained points in a game
second meaning: marked a line or incision in a surface

explanation.surface: A golfer racks up points and so qualifies for the weekend rounds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Made the cut' suggests qualifying in golf, but it is meant literally: to score is to cut a groove.
explanation.definitionFit: To score is both to gain points in a game and to scratch or cut a line into something.

clue.text: During search, one may need a jury

blocks.note: something happening during an event happens in it
a quest is a search

explanation.surface: A police hunt that might end up in front of a jury.
explanation.definitionFit: A coroner's inquiry into a death sometimes sits with a jury, so it is a hearing that may require one.

clue.text: Plain menu shop prepared

indicators.note: food that is prepared has been made up from raw ingredients, so these letters are worked into a new form

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A simple bill of fare drawn up by a café.
explanation.definitionFit: Homespun means simple and unsophisticated, so plain in style.

clue.text: New York families that keep up a dreadful racket

definitions.text: New York families that keep up a dreadful racket

blocks.clueFragment: New York families that keep up a dreadful racket
blocks.note: surface reading: noisy households disturbing the neighbours
setter's reading: a racket is a criminal enterprise, and the families are crime families

explanation.walkthrough: 'Racket' reads as noise, but it is an organised criminal scheme; the 'families' are the Mafia clans of New York.
explanation.definitionFit: The name, Italian for 'our thing', refers to the American Mafia, whose crime clans run extortion operations.

clue.text: Prophecy of old, deceptively clear?

indicators.note: something presented deceptively is not as it seems, so the word beside it is disguised by rearrangement

blocks.note: O is the standard abbreviation for old
taken as written

explanation.surface: An ancient prophecy that seems plain but is really misleading, like Delphi's famous riddling answers.
explanation.definitionFit: An oracle is a divine pronouncement or prophecy, as given at Delphi.

clue.text: Spanish PM goes to loo

blocks.note: John Major was British Prime Minister in the 1990s
can is slang for a toilet

explanation.surface: A British Prime Minister from Spain takes a bathroom break.
explanation.walkthrough: Loo is British slang for toilet.
explanation.definitionFit: Majorca is a Spanish island, so a Majorcan is Spanish by nationality, as a noun or adjective.

clue.text: A lingering quality, nothing harsh

blocks.note: the figure zero looks like the letter O
dour means stern or severe

explanation.surface: A description of some character trait that persists without being severe.
explanation.walkthrough: A smell hangs in the air, so a lingering quality is a cryptic way to describe one.
explanation.definitionFit: A smell is a sensory characteristic that hangs about a place, so an odour is a quality that lingers.

clue.text: Beat dog, no pet

indicators.note: saying there is no such thing means it must be taken away from the word before

blocks.note: a whippet is a slender racing dog
taken as written

explanation.surface: An instruction to strike a dog that is not a family animal.
explanation.definitionFit: To whip is to strike, and in cookery to whisk, both senses of the verb beat.

clue.text: Slog brings big defeat – Edgbaston's beginning a demonstration

indicators.note: the beginning of a name is its opening letter, so only that is kept

blocks.note: a rout is a crushing defeat
Edgbaston is a cricket ground in Birmingham
a protest march is a demonstration

explanation.surface: A long, hard cricket defeat at Edgbaston leads to a protest by the fans.
explanation.walkthrough: Edgbaston is England's Test cricket ground in Birmingham, so 'slog' wants to be a big hit in cricket.
explanation.definitionFit: A route march is a long, tiring military training walk, so a slog.

clue.text: Calm pupil, outwardly sharp

indicators.note: the outward part of a word is its edge, so only its two end letters are kept

blocks.note: first and last letters of the word
an acid taste or remark is sharp

explanation.surface: A composed student who nonetheless shows a sharp edge.
explanation.definitionFit: Placid means serene and untroubled, a synonym for calm.

clue.text: Rebecca is involved with spy, nothing physical in it

indicators.note: being involved means being tangled up, so these letters are mixed together

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A woman named Rebecca gets entangled with a spy in an affair that never turns physical.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nothing physical in it' sounds like a chaste relationship, but it describes a virtual world.
explanation.definitionFit: Cyberspace is the virtual realm of computer networks, a place without any material substance.

clue.text: To acquire gadget, small daughter sucked up

indicators.note: to acquire something is to take it in, so the outer letters hold the gadget inside them

blocks.note: S is the clothing-size abbreviation for small
D is the standard abbreviation for daughter
Apple's smartphone, a familiar gadget

explanation.surface: A young girl desperate to get a new device, sucking up to her parents.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sucked up' suggests fawning to get the gadget, but it means drawn up through a tube.
explanation.definitionFit: To siphon liquid is to draw it up and out through a tube by suction.

clue.text: In all honesty, be inquisitive about article of passing interest

indicators.note: about means around, so the first word is wrapped round the second

blocks.note: to pry is to be nosy
an obituary is a newspaper article about someone who has passed away

explanation.surface: Someone frankly admitting to nosiness about a mildly interesting news story.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Passing interest' sounds like casual curiosity, but 'passing' means dying: an obit is a death notice.
explanation.definitionFit: Probity is strict integrity and uprightness, a formal synonym for honesty.

clue.text: What may be afoot in coaches

blocks.note: first meaning: sports shoes worn on the feet
second meaning: people who train athletes

explanation.surface: Something suspicious going on among the passengers of long-distance buses.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Afoot' usually means happening; here it means literally on the foot. Trainers is the British word for sneakers.
explanation.definitionFit: Trainers are both running shoes worn on the feet and instructors who coach sportspeople.

clue.text: Two legs treading the boards

blocks.note: first leg: in cricket the on side is also called the leg side
second leg: a stage is one leg of a journey

explanation.surface: A description of an actor, or a biped, walking across the floorboards.
explanation.walkthrough: Each of 'Two legs' is a different synonym for leg: the on (leg) side of a cricket field, and a stage of a journey.
explanation.definitionFit: Treading the boards is an idiom for acting in the theatre, so performing in front of an audience.

clue.text: Bloomer may come to ruin game

indicators.note: what something may come to is what it turns into, so the following letters become a new word

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A blunder that could spoil a match.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bloomer' looks like a mistake, but it is a plant that blooms.
explanation.definitionFit: A geranium is a flowering garden plant, so a bloomer in the crossword sense of something that blooms.

clue.text: One freed oneself, having stuck head in three-quarters

indicators.note: something stuck in a place is lodged inside it, so one piece goes within the other

blocks.note: the quarters are compass points: east, south, east
a cape is a headland

explanation.surface: A prisoner who broke free after getting their head jammed somewhere.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Three-quarters' looks like a fraction, but the quarters are compass points; CAPE sits after the S of E, S, E.
explanation.definitionFit: An escapee is a person who has broken out of confinement, one who freed themselves.

clue.text: Top actor fights for media franchise

blocks.note: a leading actor is a star
wars are large-scale fights

explanation.surface: A leading actor battling for the rights to a film series.
explanation.definitionFit: The George Lucas space saga spans films, books, games and toys, a classic multimedia brand.

clue.text: That is Victor in the nick

indicators.note: in places the earlier pieces inside the following word

blocks.note: taken as written
i.e. is the abbreviation for 'id est', that is
Victor is V in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Pointing out a man named Victor who is in prison.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The nick' is British slang for prison, but 'nick' alone is the definition: to nick is to steal.
explanation.definitionFit: Nick is British slang for steal, the same as to thieve.

clue.text: Thin volume agreed, to a certain extent

indicators.note: only partly, so the answer is just a portion of the words before it

blocks.note: found across the two words

explanation.surface: A slim book was approved, though only with reservations.
explanation.definitionFit: Meagre means lacking in quantity or substance, scanty, which is one sense of thin.

clue.text: PM on edge in extreme disorder

blocks.note: Theresa May was British Prime Minister 2016-19
a hem is the edge of a piece of cloth

explanation.surface: A nervous Prime Minister in a chaotic government.
explanation.definitionFit: Mayhem is violent confusion and chaos, so disorder at its worst.

clue.text: Son writes in notebook where to get his meds

indicators.note: in says the preceding words are placed inside the following one

blocks.note: a diary is a notebook for daily entries
S is the standard abbreviation for son
to pen is to write

explanation.surface: A son jotting down in a notebook where his father's prescriptions can be collected.
explanation.definitionFit: A dispensary is a place where medicines are prepared and handed out, as in a pharmacy or clinic.

clue.text: Spy showing restraint

blocks.note: first meaning: Ian Fleming's secret agent 007
second meaning: a tie or shackle that binds

explanation.walkthrough: 'Restraint' suggests self-control in a secret agent, but it means a physical fetter.
explanation.definitionFit: James Bond is fiction's most famous secret agent, and a bond is a cord or chain that restrains.

clue.text: Army officer contracted for ship

indicators.note: a contracted word is shortened, so its tail is cut away

blocks.note: a brigadier commands a brigade

explanation.surface: A soldier signed up to serve on a vessel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Contracted' suggests hiring under contract; here it means shortened, and Brig is also the usual short form of the rank.
explanation.definitionFit: A brig is a two-masted square-rigged sailing vessel.

clue.text: She may run a service vehicle after 6

indicators.note: after says the following item is placed behind the one named next

blocks.note: VI is 6 in Roman numerals
a car is a vehicle

explanation.surface: A woman who operates a delivery van service, perhaps.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Service' suggests a business or vehicle maintenance, but it is a church service, led by a woman priest.
explanation.definitionFit: A vicar leads church worship, and in the Church of England may be a woman, so she runs a service.

clue.text: University tires me out – I leave as this?

indicators.note: things put out of place are disordered, so these letters get rearranged

blocks.note: U is the standard abbreviation for university
taken as written

explanation.surface: A worn-out academic wonders what title they will retire with.
explanation.definitionFit: A retiring professor often keeps an honorary title, so they depart with that status, as in professor emeritus.
